steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-07, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 2831.4 | 17.20 | 17.20
2 | 3567.9 | 2.07 | 19.27
3 | 3454.3 | 21.64 | 40.91
4 | 11701.4 | 4.12 | 45.03
5 | 140416.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-07, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-07, Survey Area T**

The interpreted VES model at T-07 comprises five layers. A shallow resistive layer (2831.4 Ω·m, 17.20 m thick) is underlain by a thin, slightly more resistive layer (3567.9 Ω·m, 2.07 m), followed by a thicker layer of comparable resistivity (3454.3 Ω·m, 21.64 m) extending to 40.91 m depth. Beneath this, resistivity increases sharply to 11701.4 Ω·m over a thin 4.12 m layer, and the sequence terminates in a very high-resistivity basal layer (140416.4 Ω·m), interpreted as the resistive basement.

Applying the standard three-layer letter convention to the resistivity sequence: layers 1-2-3 give K (r1<r2>r3), layers 2-3-4 give H (r2>r3<r4), and layers 3-4-5 give A (r3<r4<r5). This yields a KHA-type curve, consistent with the classification on file.
